PC: Defibrillate at 2-4 Joules/kg (8 kg = 16-32J, depending on rounding of defibrillator)
Resume CPR after defibrillation < 10 seconds between holding CPR and restarting
[for advanced learners] dose and draw up antiarrhythmics
First Responder: Enters the room, checks for responsiveness, sees an unresponsive patient. Shakes and shouts to make sure.
First responder feels for carotid pulse 5-10 seconds
Pulses should not be found, says “There is no pulse, I’m starting compressions” and starts compressions
Second responder becomes *airway*, gets BVM, hooks up O2, and starts coordinated CPR, remainder of team arrives
Team places stool for compressor, backboard, defibrillation pad placement, length-based tape, sets defibrillator, and charges it.
Bedside provider feels for 5-10 seconds and reports, “There is no pulse”
New *compressor* resumes CPR, Bedside Provider obtains IO access, draws up epinephrine, and gives first epinephrine dose with flush.

Bedside provider (who was first responder) checks access, draws up Epinephrine 0.01 mg/kg, 0.1 mL/kg = 0.8 mL of epinephrine. When ready, bedside provider checks dose with team lead and administers dose.
Team lead checks dose for second defibrillation (4J/kg, rounded up usually > 32 J)
MK: “I see ventricular tachycardia, this is pulseless VT, Clear the patient, on 3 I am shocking, 1,2,3, [push button]. [bedside provider] you are the new compressor, resume compressions, [airway] start 2-minute timer, [first compressor→ now bedside provider] draw up epinephrine”

“I see ventricular tachycardia, this is pulseless VT, Clear the patient, on 3 I am shocking, 1,2,3, [push button]. [bedside provider] you are the new compressor, resume compressions, [airway] start 2-minute timer, [first compressor→ now bedside provider] draw up antiarrhythmic.”
SBP: “Patient is unresponsive. I need help!” pushes code button and then gets gloves
ICS: Lead directs bedside provider into position, and for compressor to hold compressions as soon as initial priorities are finished.
Lead: “At end of cycle of 15, [bedside provider] feel for a pulse, [compressor] hold compressions and step down, I will analyze rhythm, [airway] please be ready to start 2-minute timer”
Airway and team lead should both be watching time, and at 1 minute 45 seconds, announce that there are 15 seconds remaining.
Lead directs bedside provider into position

Lead: “At end of the next cycle of 15 compressions, [bedside provider] feel for a pulse, [compressor] hold compressions and step down, I will analyze rhythm, [airway] please be ready to start 2-minute timer”
